newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican business leaders want no Pacto changes.
newsitem.headline: Mexican business leaders want no Pacto changes.

text.p: Mexican business leaders met President Ernesto Zedillo Wednesday and said they agreed that the current economic pact between government, business and labour should be extended beyond October, when it is due for renewal.

"We were in agreement with him that for the rest of this year the Alliance set last year should be maintained, with not even the smallest change to what was agreed," Carlos Abascal, head of the employer's federation Coparmex, told reporters.

Officially called the Alliance for Economic Recovery (ARE) and informally known as the "Pacto", the ARE is the latest in a series of annual trilateral accords begun in 1987 by former President Miguel de la Madrid to help foster economic stability.
The ARE set last year established tight monetary and fiscal discipline and included coordinated targets for inflation, increases in the minimum wage and hikes in gasoline and electricity prices.

Hector Larios Santillan, president of the Business Coordinating Council, said the aim of business leaders was to "reach the full implementation of the policies that were set for 1996" before the ARE is renewed.
The ARE is a key plank in the government's efforts to overcome the December 1994 peso crisis and ensuing deep recession, from which the economy is now emerging.

Organised labour, although traditionally subservient to the long-ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) and government policy, is likely to oppose efforts to extend the ARE for the rest of 1996 without further wage increases.
